intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar with Icelandic craft beer. Book the Comfort package to stay within budget while still enjoying the iconic experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views above the steam)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience offers a peaceful soak in 38–40°C water with stunning rural scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food Walk & New Nordic Tasting
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene on a self-guided tasting walk through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa), skyr desserts, freshly baked rye bread, and smoked Arctic char at local markets and eateries like Hlemmur Mathöll food hall.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide, then descend into a stunning natural ice cave with vivid blue ice formations. This bucket-list adventure combines physical activity with breathtaking geological wonder unique to Iceland.
experiences.location: Skaftafell, Vatnajökull National Park, Southeast Iceland

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives late night
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~2,500 ISK) to Reykjavík. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront accommodation. Grab a quick snack from a 24-hour petrol station convenience store (Orkan or N1) near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Convenience store snacks or instant noodles from petrol station (~500–800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy drinks or snacks in your carry-on for the late arrival. Download the Vedur.is weather app and Aurora Forecast app immediately — essential for planning northern lights outings. Exchange a small amount of currency or confirm your card works at ATMs. January in Iceland means very limited daylight (roughly 5–6 hours), so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. After a slow start, walk the Reykjavík waterfront promenade along Sæbraut. Visit the iconic Harpa Concert Hall exterior (free) and the Sun Voyager sculpture (free). Pick up groceries at Bonus supermarket (the budget traveler's best friend in Iceland) for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Reykjavík on foot. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church — climb the tower for panoramic city views (~1,000 ISK). Stroll Laugavegur shopping street window shopping. Visit the colorful old harbor area. Pop into the Reykjavík City Library (free, warm, great WiFi) to plan the rest of your trip.
day_by_day.evening: Check the Aurora Forecast app. If KP index is 3 or higher and skies are clear, head to the Grótta lighthouse on the Seltjarnarnes peninsula (free, 20-minute walk or bus from city center) for northern lights viewing away from city light pollution. Bundle up in all layers.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or cereal from Bonus supermarket at the hotel (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand — Iceland's most famous hot dog, one of the cheapest hot meals in the country (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with tomato sauce cooked in hotel kitchen or buy ready meals from Bonus (~600–900 ISK total)

day_by_day.notes: January daylight in Reykjavík is approximately 10:00–15:30. Plan all outdoor sightseeing within this window. Bonus supermarket is closed on Sundays — stock up today if needed. Wear waterproof boots and thermal layers every single day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the public Strætó bus (Route 1 or local routes, ~490 ISK per ride) toward the Reykjanes Peninsula. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) — a small footbridge spanning the gap between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walk the surrounding lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Geothermal Area and Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (free). Watch the dramatic steam vents and boiling mud. Walk the marked trails around the geothermal field. Visit the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse) nearby — free and scenic even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík by bus. Check aurora forecast. If conditions are favorable, join a free self-guided northern lights hunt at Öskjuhlíð hill (Perlan area) — elevated, dark enough, and walkable from many parts of the city. Bring a thermos of hot tea.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered eggs and toast at hotel (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches from Bonus for the day trip (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar sandwich shop in Reykjavík — affordable filled baguettes (~1,200–1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly geothermally active — stay on marked paths near all hot spring areas. Ground temperatures can be dangerously high off-trail. Bus schedules in January may be reduced — check Straeto.is the night before. Carry hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group day tour of the Golden Circle (book in advance via Reykjavík Excursions or Gray Line, ~8,000–10,000 ISK — the most cost-effective way without a rental car). First stop: Þingvellir National Park — walk the Almannagjá rift valley between tectonic plates (free entry to park, tour covers transport).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle tour: visit the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes (free entry). Then Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls, dramatic even in winter ice (free entry). Wear crampons or ice grips if available.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík by ~18:00–19:00. Warm up at the hotel. Check northern lights forecast — Golden Circle areas away from the city are prime viewing spots if the tour runs late or offers an aurora stop (ask your guide). Rest and prepare packed lunch for tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered yogurt and fruit from Bonus (~250 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel — sandwiches and snacks (~400 ISK). Avoid overpriced tourist cafés at Geysir.
meals.dinner: Noodle Station in Reykjavík — budget-friendly Asian noodle soups (~1,500–1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Golden Circle tour at least 2–3 days in advance in January. Wear your warmest clothes — wind chill at Gullfoss can be brutal. Gullfoss and Geysir parking areas have free public toilets. Bring a refillable water bottle — Icelandic tap water is among the world's purest and free everywhere.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Laugardalslaug public swimming pool and hot spring complex in Reykjavík (~1,000–1,200 ISK entry). This is the authentic Icelandic hot pot experience — outdoor geothermal pools, steam rooms, and hot tubs used by locals daily. Arrive early to enjoy it without crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take bus to Elliðaárdalur valley — a beautiful free nature reserve within Reykjavík city limits. Walk the river trail along the Elliðaár river. Visit the Árbær Open Air Museum nearby (check winter opening hours, ~1,800 ISK) — a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora hunting evening. Take bus or walk to Öskjuhlíð hill near Perlan (free). The Perlan building has a free outdoor observation deck. Stay out for 1–2 hours if skies are clear. KP index of 3+ with clear skies gives good odds in January. Photograph with a wide-angle lens or smartphone night mode.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered porridge with brown sugar — warming winter breakfast (~200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Laugardalslaug or self-catered packed lunch (~400–600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — Bonus supermarket stew or soup with bread (~700 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic swimming pool etiquette requires thorough showering without a swimsuit before entering pools — this is strictly enforced. Bring your own towel to save rental cost (~500 ISK). The pools are genuinely one of the best budget experiences in Iceland and a cultural must-do.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (book a budget group tour, ~10,000–13,000 ISK, or rent a car if splitting cost with other travelers). Morning departure. Drive through dramatic lava fields and coastal scenery. Stop at Ytri Tunga beach — known for seal colonies (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Walk the marked coastal trails around Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free). Explore the dramatic sea stacks at Lóndrangar basalt cliffs (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return drive back toward Reykjavík. The long dark drive back is an excellent opportunity for northern lights spotting from the road — ask your driver to pull over if aurora activity is detected. Return to hotel by 21:00–22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel for the day trip (~500 ISK). Limited food options on the peninsula in winter.
meals.dinner: Reykjavík Chips — Iceland's best budget fish and chips shop (~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes in January can have severe weather — check forecasts the night before. The tour may be cancelled or rerouted due to road closures (F-roads are completely closed in winter). Dress in full waterproofs. The peninsula is about 2.5–3 hours from Reykjavík. January offers the best aurora viewing odds of any month.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and Reykjavík deep dive. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around actual Viking Age ruins (~2,000 ISK). Explore the 871±2 AD longhouse remains. Then walk to the National Museum of Iceland (~2,000 ISK or free with Reykjavík City Card if purchased).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tjörnin lake in the city center — often partially frozen in January, with ducks and arctic birds. Walk to the Reykjavík Botanical Garden (free, though limited in winter). Browse the flea market at Kolaportið if it's the weekend (Saturdays and Sundays only, free entry) — great for cheap Icelandic wool goods.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated aurora evening. Take a Strætó bus to the Álftanes peninsula (30 minutes from city center) — very dark, minimal light pollution, sea views. Set up on the shore and wait. Bring a tripod for photography, hot drinks in a thermos, and hand warmers. Stay 2–3 hours if skies remain clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs and Skyr (Icelandic yogurt) from Bonus (~350 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Babalú in Reykjavík — cozy, affordable soups and sandwiches (~1,200–1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — grilled salmon from Bonus with rice and vegetables (~900 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjavík City Card (24hr ~3,900 ISK / 48hr ~5,300 ISK / 72hr ~6,900 ISK) covers most city museums and unlimited bus travel — calculate whether it saves money based on your plans. January 21 has roughly 5.5 hours of daylight. The Kolaportið flea market is a budget traveler's treasure trove for cheap Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast (book budget group tour ~9,000–12,000 ISK). Depart early. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (free entry, icy in January — crampons essential, ~500 ISK rental). Then Skógafoss waterfall — massive and dramatic with ice formations in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves (free). WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are deadly. Walk the beach carefully. Drive through the village of Vík for a quick look at the black sand coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavík. The South Coast road (Route 1) offers excellent aurora viewing on clear nights — wide open skies with minimal light pollution. Ask your guide or driver to stop if aurora is visible. Return to hotel by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from hotel (~500 ISK). Bring extra snacks — food stops are limited and expensive on the South Coast.
meals.dinner: Aktu Taktu burger restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's most affordable fast food burger chain (~1,000–1,400 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is one of Iceland's most dramatic and accessible regions. In January, Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed due to ice — check with your guide. Reynisfjara beach has claimed lives — heed all warning signs. Dress in full waterproofs; South Coast weather is notoriously unpredictable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach (free or minimal entry fee ~400 ISK in winter) — a man-made geothermal lagoon on the Reykjavík shoreline where warm water is pumped into a sheltered bay. Swim in the heated water while surrounded by winter scenery. Truly unique experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grafarvogur neighborhood and walk along the Reykjavík coastal path toward the Kársnes peninsula. Visit the Ásmundarsafn sculpture museum (part of Reykjavík Art Museum, ~1,800 ISK or free with City Card) — housed in a stunning dome building with outdoor sculpture garden.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights planning evening. Check multiple forecast apps (Vedur.is, Space Weather Live, My Aurora Forecast). If forecast is excellent (KP 4+), take a bus to Heiðmörk nature reserve on the outskirts of Reykjavík — very dark, forested, excellent aurora viewing spot. Bring a friend or join other travelers for safety.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — Skyr with granola and honey (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Mál og Menning bookstore café — affordable soups and open-faced sandwiches in a cozy setting (~1,000–1,300 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — Bonus supermarket lamb soup kit — authentic Icelandic kjötsúpa (~600 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Nauthólsvík is a genuinely magical experience — swimming in geothermal water in January with snow possibly falling around you. Bring your swimsuit and towel. The outdoor sculpture garden at Ásmundarsafn is free to wander even if you skip the museum interior. Heiðmörk is safe but bring a headlamp and fully charged phone.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Hvalfjörður fjord area by bus or rideshare. Walk the marked trail to Glymur waterfall trailhead — note that the full trail may be impassable in January ice, but the fjord scenery and lower trail are beautiful and free. The fjord is stunning in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akranes town and lighthouse (Akranesviti) accessible by bus or the Hvalfjörður tunnel. Walk the lighthouse peninsula — free and scenic. Visit the Akranes Folk Museum if open (~1,000 ISK). The drive through the undersea Hvalfjörður tunnel is an experience itself (toll ~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant as a halfway-trip reward. Check aurora forecast for late night viewing from the hotel's beachfront location — coastal areas can offer good aurora views over the water.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — toast with Icelandic butter and jam (~200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the day trip (~400 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — legendary Reykjavík harbor restaurant, famous for cheap lobster soup (~1,500 ISK per bowl) and fish skewers (~800 ISK each). Budget splurge worth every króna.

day_by_day.notes: Glymur is Iceland's second tallest waterfall but the crossing logs are removed in winter — do not attempt the full trail. The lower fjord walk is still spectacular. Hvalfjörður means 'Whale Fjord' — whale sightings are rare in January but keep an eye on the water. Dress warmly; fjord wind is cutting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Perlan (Wonders of Iceland) museum — the iconic glass dome building on Öskjuhlíð hill. The observation deck is free; the museum interior (~2,800 ISK) includes Iceland's only indoor real ice cave tunnel and northern lights planetarium show — highly recommended for a rainy or cloudy day when outdoor aurora viewing isn't possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Öskjuhlíð forest trails around Perlan — free, peaceful, and offers city panoramas. Then take bus to Kópavogur (neighboring town) to visit the Natural History Museum of Kópavogur (free or minimal entry) and browse the local shopping area for cheaper prices than central Reykjavík.
day_by_day.evening: Final serious northern lights attempt. Take a Strætó bus to Garðabær or Hafnarfjörður suburbs — darker than central Reykjavík, easy to reach by public bus. Find an open field or seafront area. January statistically offers the highest aurora activity of the year. Stay out until midnight if conditions are good.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — full Icelandic-style breakfast with eggs, skyr, and rye bread (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Kópavogur mall food court — cheaper than Reykjavík city center (~1,000–1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered — Bonus supermarket fish pie or ready meal (~700 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan northern lights planetarium show is worth it on cloudy nights when real aurora isn't visible — it gives you the full visual experience with educational content. The indoor ice cave is genuinely impressive. Öskjuhlíð hill is also one of the best free outdoor aurora viewing spots in the city due to its elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated hot springs day. Visit Laugarvatn Fontana geothermal baths (~4,500 ISK) — a beautiful lakeside spa with natural steam saunas built directly over geothermal vents, and outdoor pools overlooking Lake Laugarvatn. Accessible by day tour or rental car. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Fontana, visit the nearby Laugarvatn village and walk along the lake shore (free). If on a tour, it may include a stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, more rustic and affordable than the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry), surrounded by active geothermal vents and bubbling hot springs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Final aurora attempt from the hotel's beachfront location — step outside and look north. Pack bags for tomorrow's activities and begin organizing for departure. Reflect on the trip over a warm Icelandic hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure (~300 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café at Laugarvatn Fontana or packed lunch (~500–800 ISK). The rye bread baked in the geothermal ground at Fontana with butter is a must-try (~600 ISK).
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner — Hamborgarabúllan (The Burger Joint) in Reykjavík — best burgers in Iceland, reasonable prices (~1,800–2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK vs ~12,000+ ISK) and offers a more authentic, less touristy experience. Pre-booking is essential for both venues. The geothermal rye bread (hverabrauð) baked underground at Fontana is one of Iceland's most unique food experiences — do not skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up early and take one last walk along the beachfront near the hotel — watch the winter sunrise over the ocean (around 10:30 in January). Visit a local bakery for a traditional Icelandic pastry — try a skúffukaka (chocolate sponge cake) or kleina (twisted doughnut) from Sandholt Bakery (~500–700 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage if possible. Final stroll down Laugavegur for any last-minute souvenir shopping — budget picks include Icelandic sea salt (~1,000 ISK), dried fish snacks (harðfiskur, ~800 ISK), or a small lava rock (free from the ground, but do not remove from national parks). Head to Keflavík Airport via Flybus (~2,500 ISK, book in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of hot springs, aurora hunting, waterfalls, geothermal landscapes, and Viking history — all on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Sandholt Bakery pastry and coffee — a perfect final Reykjavík morning (~700–900 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or final Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog before heading to the bus (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the Flybus journey plus airport check-in and security. Flybus departs from BSÍ bus terminal in Reykjavík — confirm your pickup time when booking. Duty-free alcohol at Keflavík Airport is significantly cheaper than anywhere in Iceland — a popular final purchase for many travelers. January budget estimate for the full 13 days excluding flights and accommodation: approximately 80,000–110,000 ISK (~€550–€760 EUR) covering transport, activities, and self-catered meals.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel. If hungry, grab a light snack at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the hotel bar or room service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: January nights in Iceland are long and dark — ideal for northern lights. Keep an eye on the aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) right from night one. Dress warmly; January temperatures hover around -2°C to 4°C.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to breathe in the fresh Icelandic coastal air and acclimate to the surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik city center (approx. 45-min drive) for the Reykjavik Food Walk & New Nordic Tasting. Explore the city's vibrant culinary scene, sampling Icelandic lamb soup, skyr, rye bread, and local seafood bites at various stops around the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Check the northern lights forecast. If aurora activity is predicted (KP index 2+), step outside the hotel or nearby dark coastal spots for your first potential northern lights viewing. The beachfront location offers low light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Reykjavik Food Walk
meals.dinner: Grillið or Messinn in Reykjavik — try the pan-fried Arctic char or lamb fillet (mid-range, ~3,500–5,500 ISK per main)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a local SIM card or confirm roaming coverage today. Download the Vedur.is aurora forecast app and set alerts. January sunlight is limited to about 5–6 hours (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — located just 20 minutes from the hotel near Grindavík. Book the Comfort package (pre-booking essential). Arrive early to enjoy the milky-blue silica-rich waters, in-water silica mud mask, and algae mask before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at the Blue Lagoon. Enjoy the steam caves, sauna, and waterfall massage features. Have lunch at the Lava Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon complex — a mid-range splurge with stunning views over the geothermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by late afternoon. Rest and recharge. Check the aurora forecast — if conditions are favorable, bundle up and head to a dark coastal area near the resort for northern lights viewing with hot drinks from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — fish of the day or Icelandic lamb burger (~4,500–6,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel restaurant — Icelandic fish stew or lamb soup to warm up after a full spa day

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked well in advance, especially in winter. The Comfort package includes one drink, silica mud mask, and algae mask. Bring a hair tie — the silica minerals can tangle hair. Swimsuit rental available on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the famous Golden Circle route. Start with Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Stunning winter scenery with frost-covered lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–40 meters into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most iconic cascades, dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the hotel. Stop at a local petrol station for a famous Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) — a beloved budget snack. Arrive at the hotel, check aurora forecast, and if skies are clear, join the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour departing from the Reykjavik area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — pack a thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café near Strokkur — lamb soup and Icelandic meat pie (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Faxi Restaurant near Gullfoss or Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — fresh trout from the local lake (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the hotel. Roads in January can be icy — check road conditions at Road.is before departing. Wear microspike traction cleats near Gullfoss as paths can be very slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the hotel. Sleep in after potentially a late northern lights tour the previous night. Enjoy breakfast and take a peaceful walk along the beachfront. Review photos and plan the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for a self-guided exploration of the dramatic volcanic landscape. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free), the Reykjanes Lighthouse, and the fumarole fields at Gunnuhver Hot Springs — Iceland's largest hot spring area with boiling mud pools and steam vents.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for dinner. Northern lights check — if KP index is favorable, drive 10 minutes from the hotel to a dark coastal viewpoint for aurora watching. Bring a tripod if you have one for long-exposure photography.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop in Grindavík — local bakery with Icelandic pastries and soup (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — grilled fish of the day with Icelandic butter sauce and roasted root vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver Hot Springs are powerful and steaming — stay on marked paths at all times. The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically very active; check for any volcanic alerts at Vedur.is before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the long drive to South Iceland. Head east along Route 1 (Ring Road) toward Vík. Stop at Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy in January, use caution). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall for sweeping winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — dramatic basalt column formations, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the iconic Dyrhólaey arch viewpoint for panoramic coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or hotel in Vík for the night (pre-book: Hotel Kría or Puffin Hotel Vík). Enjoy dinner in town and check the aurora forecast — Vík's remote location away from city lights makes it excellent for northern lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departing
meals.lunch: Picnic or café stop at Skógar Museum café near Skógafoss (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi in Vík — lamb burger or fish and chips with a local Víking beer (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous and have caused fatalities. Seljalandsfoss path behind the waterfall may be closed in icy conditions. Drive carefully on Route 1; black ice is common in January.

day_by_day.morning: Drive further east to Skaftafell (part of Vatnajökull National Park). Meet your guide for the Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull — strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into a stunning natural ice cave beneath the glacier — marvel at the deep blue ice formations, tunnels, and chambers carved by meltwater. This is one of Iceland's most extraordinary winter-only experiences. Ice caves are only safely accessible November–March.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (30 min east of Skaftafell) for the magical blue hour and early evening light reflecting off floating icebergs. Check into accommodation near Jökulsárlón (Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon or Hali Country Hotel) and scan the skies for aurora.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Vík guesthouse before departing
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the glacier tour or café at Skaftafell visitor center (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hali Country Hotel restaurant — traditional Icelandic lamb roast or reindeer stew (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike and ice cave tour must be pre-booked with a certified guide company (e.g., Local Guide, Glacier Guides). All equipment including crampons, helmets, and harnesses are provided. The ice cave location changes each season — guides will direct you to the current accessible cave.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon at sunrise (around 11:00 in January) for the iconic 'Diamond Beach' — icebergs washed ashore on the black sand beach glittering like diamonds in the low winter light. Spend time photographing and exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the long drive back west along the Ring Road. Stop at the turf farm ruins at Núpsstaður and the beautiful Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon (if road conditions allow) — a dramatic 100-meter-deep gorge carved by glacial floods.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a relaxing evening, soak in the hotel's facilities, and celebrate the halfway point of the trip. Northern lights check before bed.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the guesthouse near Jökulsárlón
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at a petrol station or packed lunch — Icelandic hot dogs, skyr, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Welcome back dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — splurge slightly on a celebratory Icelandic tasting menu with local seafood and lamb

day_by_day.notes: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon road (Route F206) may be closed in winter — check road.is. The drive from Jökulsárlón back to the hotel is approximately 4–5 hours; start no later than 13:00 to arrive before full darkness.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and leisure morning at the hotel. Enjoy the hotel's spa or pool facilities. Take a slow breakfast and review the week's photos. Light stretching or yoga session to recover from the glacier hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (approx. 1.5 hours from the hotel). Soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool — a natural hot spring dating to 1891 surrounded by a geothermal landscape with small geysers bubbling nearby. Far less crowded than Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Dinner near the hotel. Check aurora forecast — if conditions are strong tonight, the Secret Lagoon area or the drive back through rural Iceland offers excellent dark-sky opportunities. Consider pulling over on a clear road for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — relaxed and unhurried
meals.lunch: Café Mika in Flúðir near the Secret Lagoon — homemade Icelandic soup and fresh-baked bread (~2,000–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or a local restaurant near the resort — pan-seared cod with capers and brown butter (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon costs approximately 2,800–3,200 ISK per adult — much more affordable than Blue Lagoon. No booking required but advisable in winter. The water temperature is a constant 38–40°C. Bring a swimsuit and towel (rental available). The surrounding mini-geysers erupt every few minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavik for a full day of culture. Visit Hallgrímskirkja Church (take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views), then explore the National Museum of Iceland to learn about Viking history and Icelandic culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Laugavegur shopping street — browse local design shops, wool sweater stores (lopapeysa), and independent boutiques. Visit Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront for its stunning geometric glass architecture. Explore the Old Harbor area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavik's nightlife scene. Start with cocktails at Slippbarinn at Harpa or Kaldi Bar. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range Reykjavik restaurant. Return to the hotel — check aurora forecast on the drive back for potential roadside viewing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland, a Reykjavik institution (~500 ISK) followed by coffee at Reykjavik Roasters
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik — French-Icelandic fusion with excellent fish soup and lamb main (~4,000–6,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hallgrímskirkja tower costs approximately 1,000 ISK — worth every krona for the view. The National Museum of Iceland costs ~2,000 ISK. Reykjavik is very walkable — park the car near the hotel and explore on foot. January evenings in Reykjavik are lively despite the cold.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour tonight (or confirm existing booking). During the day, visit the Reykjanes area again for the Bridge Between Continents and the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark visitor center to learn about the peninsula's volcanic history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the hotel — use the spa, pool, or simply read and nap in preparation for a late-night northern lights tour. Pack warm layers, hand warmers, and a hot drink thermos for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — join a small-group guided jeep tour departing from the Reykjavik/Keflavík area. Expert guides drive away from light pollution using real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to find the best viewing spots. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00 or 22:00–01:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a café near Grindavík — fish soup and bread
meals.dinner: Early dinner at the hotel before the tour — hearty lamb stew or beef burger to fuel the cold night ahead (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights Jeep tours cost approximately 9,000–14,000 ISK per person. Most operators offer a free rebooking if aurora activity is too low. Dress in your warmest layers — standing outside in January winds at -5°C to -10°C can be brutal. Hand warmers are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in after the late northern lights tour. Late breakfast at the hotel. Spend time reviewing and editing your best aurora photographs. Pack non-essential items and begin organizing luggage for the final day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final exploration drive: Visit the Krýsuvík geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula — colorful hot spring vents, boiling mud pools, and steaming fumaroles in a surreal volcanic landscape. Free to visit. Then stop at the picturesque Lake Kleifarvatn nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant. Celebrate the end of an incredible Iceland trip. If skies are clear, do one final aurora watch from the hotel's beachfront — a perfect ending to the journey.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a stop at a local bakery on the Reykjanes drive
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — splurge on the full Icelandic tasting menu: Greenlandic shrimp, smoked lamb, skyr dessert with crowberries (~6,000–8,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Krýsuvík is free to visit but stay strictly on boardwalks — the ground around hot springs is thin and scalding water lies just beneath the surface. Lake Kleifarvatn is eerie and beautiful in winter light. Check road.is before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last full Icelandic breakfast at the hotel. Take a short beachfront walk to soak in the Icelandic coastal scenery one final time. Check out of the hotel and load luggage into the car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, stop at the Blue Lagoon for one final soak (book in advance) — it is located directly on the route to Keflavík Airport, making it a perfect final activity. Alternatively, browse the duty-free shops at Keflavík Airport for Icelandic souvenirs: Icelandic wool items, lava salt, Brennivín schnapps, and skyr.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 unforgettable days of northern lights, geothermal hot springs, glaciers, waterfalls, and Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the skyr and smoked salmon one last time
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon café or Keflavík Airport restaurants — fish and chips or Icelandic lamb wrap (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping at Keflavík Airport. The Blue Lagoon is only 15–20 minutes from the airport — if time allows, a 2-hour soak is the perfect farewell to Iceland. Return rental car before the Blue Lagoon stop if applicable.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir National Park, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask ritual, and a swim-up bar with Icelandic craft beer. Book the Comfort package to stay within budget while still enjoying the iconic experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views above the steam)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot pools. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience offers a peaceful soak in 38–40°C water with stunning rural scenery.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food Walk & New Nordic Tasting
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene on a self-guided tasting walk through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa), skyr desserts, freshly baked rye bread, and smoked Arctic char at local markets and eateries like Hlemmur Mathöll food hall.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide, then descend into a stunning natural ice cave with vivid blue ice formations. This bucket-list adventure combines physical activity with breathtaking geological wonder unique to Iceland.
experiences.location: Skaftafell, Vatnajökull National Park, Southeast Iceland

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome glass of Champagne prepared by the concierge, and settle into your beachfront suite. Light room-service supper and rest.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Private room-service at Aegean Bliss Resort – smoked lamb soup, Icelandic skyr parfait, herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before arrival. Pre-book private airport transfer. Request early check-in preparation from resort so the room is warm and turndown service is ready upon arrival. Pack layers for immediate cold-weather exposure on exit from airport.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a lavish resort breakfast with panoramic ocean views. Explore the resort grounds, beachfront hot tub, and geothermal pool at leisure. Receive a briefing from the resort concierge on the full 13-day program.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa – just 10 minutes from the resort. Arrive for a private Retreat Spa package: soak in the iconic milky-blue silica-rich waters, receive an in-water floating massage, silica mud mask ritual, and algae mask treatment. Enjoy a private changing suite and complimentary sparkling wine at the in-water bar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Freshen up and dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Tonight's Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep departs at 21:00 – a small-group guided expedition into the Reykjanes Peninsula wilderness to escape light pollution. Expert guide monitors aurora forecasts in real time. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet – fresh-baked rye bread, smoked salmon, Icelandic dairy, seasonal fruits, Americano
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant – langoustine bisque, pan-seared Arctic char, skyr cheesecake
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort fine-dining – slow-roasted lamb rack, root vegetable purée, Icelandic moss butter, paired wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat package well in advance – slots fill quickly. Northern Lights tour is weather-dependent; the guide will confirm go/no-go by 19:00. Dress in thermal base layers plus the resort-provided insulated oversuit for the jeep tour.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast. Guided beachfront walk along the Reykjanes coastal lava fields with a private naturalist guide – witness dramatic sea-cliff formations, birdlife, and the raw volcanic landscape unique to the peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Reykjavik (45 minutes). Reykjavik Food Walk & New Nordic Tasting – a curated self-guided premium tasting route through the city center. Sample fermented shark (hákarl), smoked puffin canapés, lamb meatballs, craft Icelandic spirits, and artisan skyr at hand-picked vendors. Explore Hallgrímskirkja church and Harpa Concert Hall exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (brief, ~15:30) viewing from Perlan observation deck. Dinner at Dill Restaurant (Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) – a hyper-local New Nordic tasting menu. Return by private transfer to resort. Optional late-night aurora watch from resort hot tub with aurora alert app.

meals.breakfast: Resort – Icelandic oatmeal with crowberries, poached eggs on rye, fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Food walk tastings serve as a progressive lunch across Reykjavik
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant – 7-course New Nordic tasting menu with Icelandic wine and aquavit pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Dill Restaurant reservation at least 6–8 weeks in advance. Confirm private driver for Reykjavik day. Perlan observation deck is free; consider the Northern Lights planetarium show inside Perlan as an add-on.

day_by_day.morning: Resort spa morning – full-body volcanic stone massage and geothermal facial using Icelandic mineral products. Breakfast delivered to suite. Debrief with concierge on upcoming glacier excursion logistics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private scenic drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (2.5 hours). Stop at Eldborg volcanic crater viewpoint and Ytri-Tunga beach to spot Atlantic grey seals resting on the shore. Check into a pre-arranged premium guesthouse near Snæfellsjökull for the overnight stay.
day_by_day.evening: Guided snowcat ride to the rim of Snæfellsjökull glacier at dusk for panoramic Atlantic views. Return to guesthouse for a private chef dinner featuring local catch. Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – second opportunity; the Snæfellsnes Peninsula offers outstanding dark-sky conditions with zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: In-suite at Aegean Bliss Resort – continental spread with Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Stykkishólmur – fresh langoustine soup at Narfeyrarstofa restaurant
meals.dinner: Private chef at Snæfellsnes guesthouse – pan-fried cod with roe butter, lamb stew, Icelandic flatbread, skyr panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Overnight luggage: pack a single bag for 2 nights away from the main resort. Confirm snowcat glacier ride booking (weather/visibility dependent). Keep aurora alert notifications active throughout the night.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for potential dawn aurora display over the Atlantic. Hearty breakfast at guesthouse. Guided hike through the Snæfellsjökull National Park lava tube caves (Vatnshellir cave) with a certified guide – descend 35 meters into an 8,000-year-old lava tube with dramatic geological formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic coastal drive along the southern Snæfellsnes shore: Arnarstapi basalt arch sea stacks, Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach, and Londrangar volcanic plugs. Return drive toward Reykjavik with a stop at the Deildartunguhver hot spring (Europe's highest-flow hot spring) in Borgarnes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Unwind in resort geothermal pools. Quiet fine-dining dinner at the resort with a focus on rest before the upcoming South Coast adventure.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse – scrambled eggs, smoked trout, rye bread, Icelandic butter and jam
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic hamper from guesthouse – prepared cheeses, cured meats, thermos of lamb broth, fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – pan-seared halibut, fennel cream, dill oil, Icelandic potato gratin, white Burgundy pairing

day_by_day.notes: Vatnshellir cave tour requires helmets and headlamps (provided). Deildartunguhver hot spring stop is a quick 20-minute visit – not a bathing spring, viewing only. Arrive at resort by 20:00 to enjoy pool time before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Departure by private 4WD toward the South Coast (3-hour drive via Ring Road). En route, stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall – walk behind the curtain of water (icy in January; crampons provided). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Vík. Explore the black sand beach of Reynisfjara and the basalt sea stacks of Reynisdrangar. Visit the iconic Reyniskirkja church on the hillside. Check in at a pre-arranged luxury lodge near Vík for the overnight.
day_by_day.evening: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull – depart at 17:00 with a certified glaciologist guide. Strap on crampons and explore the glacier surface under headlamps, then descend into a crystal-blue ice cave. Return by 21:00. Warm up with hot drinks and a hearty lodge dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort – smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed green juice, coffee
meals.lunch: Skógafoss Café stop – lamb soup, Icelandic brown bread, hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Vík luxury lodge – braised short rib of Icelandic beef, root vegetable medley, red wine reduction, skyr mousse with bilberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves – stay well back from the water's edge. Ice cave tour is weather and safety dependent; guide confirms viability on the day. Book Vatnajökull glacier experience at least 4 weeks ahead. Dress in resort-provided glacier gear (full waterproof suit, crampons, helmet).

day_by_day.morning: Dawn aurora possibility from lodge – wake-up call at 06:30 if aurora alert is active. Breakfast at lodge. Morning visit to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (1 hour east of Vík) – witness enormous blue icebergs calving from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier into the lagoon. Private boat tour (amphibious vessel) among the icebergs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Beach directly across from Jökulsárlón – translucent ice chunks washed onto black sand create a surreal diamond-like landscape. Photography session with a private guide. Drive back west along the Ring Road, stopping at Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon – a 2-million-year-old river canyon with dramatic curved walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Resort spa: Nordic sauna ritual (sauna, cold plunge, steam room cycle). Dinner at resort. Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – third opportunity, departing at 21:30.

meals.breakfast: Lodge – Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with jam and cream, eggs, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed luxury hamper for glacier lagoon – artisan sandwiches, thermos of tomato bisque, Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – roasted Arctic char, citrus beurre blanc, sautéed sea vegetables, Chablis pairing

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón amphibious boat tours operate year-round but are brief in winter (30 min). Fjaðrárgljúfur canyon path may be icy – trekking poles recommended. Allow 5–5.5 hours total driving today; depart lodge by 08:00.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and resort morning. Full-body hot stone massage at the resort spa. Late breakfast with ocean views. Concierge check-in to review remaining itinerary and confirm all remaining bookings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (1.5 hours northeast). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool – a naturally heated spring pool at 38–40°C, surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Small-group, intimate atmosphere far from the crowds. Champagne service at poolside arranged by resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic drive back via the Golden Circle route. Stop at Geysir geothermal area for the Strokkur geyser eruption (every 5–10 minutes). Dinner at Friðheimar tomato farm restaurant (unique greenhouse dining). Return to resort by 21:30. Aurora watch from the resort hot tub.

meals.breakfast: Resort – bircher muesli, poached eggs, smoked lamb, freshly baked sourdough, flat white
meals.lunch: Flúðir village – light snack at a local bakery, skyr and rye bread
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Restaurant – tomato soup, tomato-based lamb meatballs, tomato sorbet dessert (all grown in the greenhouse), paired with house Bloody Mary

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon is clothing-required (swimsuit). Water temperature is natural and consistent. Book Champagne poolside service directly with resort concierge 48 hours ahead. Friðheimar is a unique experience – book reservation in advance as it fills quickly even in January.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snowmobile tour on Langjökull glacier (2 hours from resort). Drive up onto Iceland's second-largest glacier by super-jeep, then ride snowmobiles across the vast white expanse with panoramic views. Descend into the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey via Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) – walk the Almannagjá rift valley, straddling the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Private guide explains Iceland's geological and Viking parliamentary history. Visit Öxará river and Drekkingarhylur pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by 18:00. Sunset cocktails at the resort bar overlooking the Atlantic. Reservation at a premium Reykjavik restaurant (Matur og Drykkur – traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined). Private transfer to and from Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Resort – full Icelandic hot breakfast: fried eggs, smoked lamb sausage, baked beans, rye toast, fresh juice
meals.lunch: Packed thermos lunch on glacier – lamb stew in a flask, premium trail mix, hot coffee
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik – cod's head dish, fermented skate, traditional lamb soup, Icelandic craft beer pairing

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tour requires minimum age 18 and valid driving licence for solo riding. Þingvellir is best explored on foot – wear insulated, waterproof boots. Book Matur og Drykkur well in advance; it is one of Reykjavik's most sought-after tables.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort wellness morning. Guided sunrise yoga session in the resort's heated glass pavilion overlooking the ocean (07:30). Spa treatment: volcanic mud wrap and mineral bath. Extended brunch at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided birdwatching and wildlife tour along the Reykjanes Peninsula coastline – spot wintering seabirds, Arctic foxes, and the Bridge Between Continents (where you can literally step between two tectonic plates). Visit the Gunnuhver mud pools and hot springs on the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by 17:00. Enjoy the resort's private geothermal infinity pool as dusk falls. Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – fourth opportunity, departing at 21:00. Upon return, hot cocoa and Icelandic schnapps nightcap in the resort lounge.

meals.breakfast: Resort – extended brunch: smoked salmon platter, avocado on rye, Icelandic waffles with cream and jam, mimosas
meals.lunch: Reykjanes Peninsula – thermos of fish chowder and artisan bread from resort kitchen
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – whole roasted Icelandic lamb shoulder, wild herb crust, roasted root vegetables, Rioja pairing

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver mud pools are extremely hot – stay strictly on boardwalks. Arctic fox sightings are possible but not guaranteed in January. Confirm aurora jeep tour go/no-go at 19:00 with guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Reykjavik for a cultural morning. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Viking and settlement-era history. Explore the old harbour district and the Kolaportið flea market for Icelandic souvenirs and local delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whale watching cruise from Reykjavik Old Harbour (winter season offers humpback and minke whale sightings). Premium vessel with heated indoor cabin, expert marine biologist guide, and complimentary hot drinks. Return to harbour by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Reykjavik luxury shopping: 101 Hotel boutique area for Icelandic wool (lopapeysa sweaters), lava jewellery, and design goods. Dinner at Ox (underground tasting counter by Dill chefs) – an ultra-exclusive 10-seat omakase-style Nordic menu. Return to resort by 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Resort – smoked trout hash, poached eggs, Icelandic flatbread, espresso
meals.lunch: Reykjavik harbour – fresh lobster roll at Sægreifinn (Sea Baron), Icelandic lamb skewers
meals.dinner: Ox Restaurant, Reykjavik – 10-course omakase Nordic tasting menu, premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching is weather-dependent; operator will notify of cancellation. Book Ox Restaurant weeks in advance – only 10 seats available. Kolaportið market is open weekends only; confirm it is open on this date.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour of the Reykjanes volcanic zone (departs from resort helipad or nearby Keflavík) – fly over active lava fields, volcanic craters, geothermal vents, and the dramatic coastline. Land on a remote lava plateau for a Champagne toast. Approximately 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort. Final Blue Lagoon visit – this time the exclusive Retreat by Blue Lagoon experience: private lagoon, in-water dining, holistic body ritual, and access to the underground lava spa. A deeper, more exclusive experience than the standard lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest table – private dining room reserved for the evening. Chef's special 8-course tasting menu celebrating Icelandic cuisine at its finest. Sommelier-led wine pairing. After dinner, final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – fifth and final opportunity, with the guide pulling out all stops for the last night.

meals.breakfast: Resort – Champagne breakfast in suite: croissants, smoked salmon, fruit platter, fresh OJ
meals.lunch: The Retreat at Blue Lagoon – in-water dining: lobster ceviche, seaweed salad, sparkling mineral water
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort private dining – 8-course farewell tasting menu: langoustine crudo, smoked puffin, reindeer tartare, glacier water sorbet, Icelandic lamb two ways, aged skyr cheese course, volcanic chocolate lava cake, petit fours; paired with premium Icelandic and European wines

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tour must be booked 2–3 weeks in advance; weather cancellation policy applies. The Retreat by Blue Lagoon requires separate premium booking from the standard lagoon. Confirm final aurora tour at 20:00 with guide. Request photographer for the evening if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Final resort breakfast at leisure with ocean views. Pack and prepare for departure. Last soak in the resort's geothermal pool. Resort concierge arranges luggage handling and departure gifts (Icelandic wool blanket, artisan skyr, lava salt, and a curated photo book of the trip if pre-ordered).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (10–15 minutes). Early airport arrival for premium lounge access. Duty-free shopping for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín aquavit), Nói Síríus chocolate, and lopapeysa wool goods.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, geothermal wonders, volcanic landscapes, and world-class Nordic cuisine.

meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport premium lounge – light bites, Icelandic beers, and snacks
meals.dinner: In-flight or airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00; request late check-out (14:00) if needed depending on flight departure time.
